question.text: Aravalli Growth Fund (Category II, close-ended) plans to list its units on BSE for liquidity. Per SEBI (AIF) Regulations, which of the following conditions applies?

answer.text: Listing is mandatory for all close-ended AIFs within 90 days of first close
Listing is permitted immediately after in-principle approval from SEBI
Listing is VOLUNTARY; minimum tradable lot INR 1 crore; listing permitted only AFTER final close; Angel Fund units cannot be listed
Minimum tradable lot is INR 10 crore; only Cat I may list

explanation.text: The Logic: Voluntary listing of close-ended AIF units is permitted only after final close, with a minimum tradable lot of INR 1 crore, and requires SEBI approval followed by stock-exchange approval. Units of Angel Funds and CDMDF cannot be listed. The Trap: Option A mandates listing (false). Option B jumps to the in-principle phase (too early). Option D fabricates the lot size and Category restriction. Note: Workbook pages 334-335 support the close-ended listing mechanics; page 354 supports Angel Fund non-listing; page 359 supports CDMDF non-listing.
